Let H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k. Asymptotic H_n = ln n + γ + 1/(2n) + ...

Compute (π^n+e^n)^{1/n}. Since π ≈ 3.14159, e≈2.71828, π > e. Factor π^n: π^n(1+(e/π)^n). 1/n power: π (1+(e/π)^n)^{1/n}. Since e/π < 1, (e/π)^n →0. Need asymptotic of (1+x_n)^{1/n} with x_n = (e/π)^n. For small x, (1+x)^{1/n} = exp((1/n) ln(1+x)) = exp((1/n)(x + O(x^2))). Since x=(e/π)^n decays exponentially, (1/n)x → 0. So exp(0) →1. Thus (π^n+e^n)^{1/n} → π.
More precise: = π * exp(O((e/π)^n/n)) = π(1 + o(1)).
Thus denominator ~ π ln n. Numerator ~ ln n. Ratio ~ 1/π.

So limit = 1/π.

Let's ensure no subtlety: numerator is harmonic sum ~ ln n + γ. Divided by ln n tends to 1. Denominator: (π^n+e^n)^{1/n} ln n / ln n → π. So overall 1/π.

answer_text:
We want

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}.
\]

Let

\[
H_n=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n.
\]

It is well known that the harmonic numbers satisfy

\[
H_n=\ln n+\gamma+o(1),
\]

so

\[
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}=1+\frac{\gamma+o(1)}{\ln n}\to 1.
\]

Now consider

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}.
\]

Since \(\pi>e\), we factor out \(\pi^n\):

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}
=\left(\pi^n\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)\right)^{1/n}
=\pi\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}.
\]

Because \(0<e/\pi<1\), we have \((e/\pi)^n\to 0\). Therefore

\[
\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}\to 1,
\]

and hence

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\to \pi.
\]

Thus the whole expression is

\[
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}\cdot \frac{1}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}}
\to 1\cdot \frac{1}{\pi}
=\frac{1}{\pi}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\pi}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Asymptotic analysis of the harmonic sum (numerator ~ ln n) and the n-th root of the exponential sum (denominator ~ π ln n), yielding ratio 1/π.
